description: From defk-7a6 (merged). In a case guard such as rem(n, y) < n * n with y = 0 and n * n overflowing i64, native raises ArithmeticError (overflow is a limit) while Elixir mode's try/rescue sees the zero divisor first and makes the guard false, so the two modes disagree. Documented in docs/language.md as a known edge; not covered by an agreement test (only the overflow-first order is). Fix: Elixir mode should apply the limit check for every operand of the guard before deciding false (e.g. evaluate with limit-checked ops that collect both flags, raise if any limit flag is set, as native's govf replay does), or native should treat a guard containing a real guard error as false regardless of overflow order if that matches Elixir. Done when an agreement test with y = 0 and an overflowing n * n passes in both orders.
title: Elixir mode returns false where native raises: a guard with both a zero divisor and an i64 overflow
